plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.7.13
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to use Pappus' Theorem to find the volume of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about an axis at distance a from the center of the circle. The figure shows a 3D torus in perspective with the vertical axis of revolution passing through its central hole; the distance a from the axis to the center of the circular cross-section and the radius b of the cross-section are labeled, with the cross-section highlighted as a small circle on the right side of the torus. A red dashed ellipse traces the circular path traveled by the centroid, with direction arrows, and a caption box reads The centroid travels a distance 2pi a. The figure shows that by Pappus' Theorem the volume V = (2 pi a)(pi b^2) = 2 pi^2 a b^2, since the centroid traverses a full circle of circumference 2 pi a as the region revolves.

elements: gray shaded torus generated by revolving a circular disk around a vertical axis
vertical black axis of revolution passing through the torus hole and extending above and below the torus
right-side generating circular disk of radius b, filled pale yellow and outlined in blue
red centroid point at the center of the generating circle
black point on the axis at the same height as the centroid
double-headed black dimension arrow from the axis point to the centroid labeled a
double-headed black dimension arrow from the centroid to the right edge of the generating circle labeled b
red dashed circular centroid path around the vertical axis, projected as an ellipse in the view
red arrowheads placed on the dashed centroid path to show direction of travel
cream-colored callout box with gray border reading 'The centroid travels a distance 2πa.'
large cream-colored callout arrow pointing from the caption box toward the red centroid path
reactive formula panel showing V = 2π²ab² and S = 4π²ab with current numeric values

interactions.label: Major radius a
interactions.teaches: Increasing a moves the generating circle farther from the axis, lengthening the centroid path 2πa and increasing both the torus volume and surface area proportionally

interactions.label: Tube radius b
interactions.teaches: Increasing b enlarges the circular generating region; volume grows with b squared while surface area grows linearly with b

interactions.label: Revolve generating circle
interactions.teaches: The torus is formed by sweeping the circular region around the axis, and the circle's centroid travels one full circumference of length 2πa
Rotating the view reveals that the red dashed ellipse is actually a horizontal circle around the vertical axis and that the shaded object is a full torus

demo_steps.title: Default torus
demo_steps.narration: The circular region of radius b sits a distance a from the vertical axis. Its centroid is the red point, and its full path is the red dashed circle of circumference 2πa.

demo_steps.title: Move the circle farther out
demo_steps.narration: Increasing a expands the red centroid path while leaving the tube thickness unchanged. By Pappus's theorem, both V = 2π²ab² and S = 4π²ab increase in direct proportion to a.

demo_steps.title: Thicken the tube
demo_steps.narration: Increasing b enlarges the generating circle. The surface area increases linearly with b, but the volume increases faster because the generating disk area is πb².

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use world coordinates with the axis of revolution as the +Y vertical axis, +X screen-right at the default view, and +Z depth. Torus centered at origin with symmetry axis along Y. Default major radius a = 2.6 and tube radius b = 0.7; torus parametric surface: x = (a + b cos v) cos u, y = b sin v, z = (a + b cos v) sin u. Overall default torus diameter is about 6.6 units and vertical tube height is 1.4 units. The generating disk is shown at the right side initially, centered at (a, 0, 0), lying in the vertical radial plane z = 0, with radius b. Disk fill pale cream/yellow #ffe3aa at about 0.75 opacity; disk outline blue #139bd7, thickness visibly heavier than dimension lines. Torus body is light gray/silver #d8d8d8 with smooth lighting, subtle darker gray shading at inner rim, and slight transparency or matte shading so the highlighted disk reads as the generating cross-section. Vertical axis is black/dark gray #222222, thin cylinder or line, extending from y = -2.2 to y = 2.2 through x = z = 0. Axis point is black sphere radius about 0.09 at (0,0,0). Centroid point is red #f4545d sphere radius about 0.1 at (a,0,0). Dimension a is a black double-headed arrow from (0,0,0) to (a,0,0), slightly offset toward camera by z = -0.03 so it remains visible, labeled italic 'a' near the center above the arrow. Dimension b is a black double-headed arrow from (a,0,0) to (a+b,0,0), labeled italic 'b' above and to the right. Red centroid path is the circle x = a cos u, y = 0, z = a sin u, rendered dashed in red #f4545d with two or three solid red arrowheads tangent to the path; in the default camera it should resemble the dashed red ellipse in the source. Caption callout is a 2D overlay or billboard near the bottom: cream fill #ffe6b5, gray border #bfbfbf, black text 'The centroid travels\na distance 2πa.' with a broad cream arrow pointing upward toward the lower-right segment of the dashed path. Formula panel should display live values: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab² and S = (2πa)(2πb) = 4π²ab; show current numerical values to 2 decimals.
interactionPlan.notes: Regenerate or rescale the torus mesh, centroid path, generating disk, dimension arrows, and formula values reactively when either slider changes. During the revolve animation, move the highlighted generating disk around the Y-axis with center (a cos θ, 0, a sin θ), rotate its plane so it remains radial, and move the red centroid point with it; keep the dashed red full path visible at all times, optionally brightening the portion already traced. Use smooth Phong or standard material lighting for the gray torus and render labels as billboarding text so they remain readable while dragging the view.

authoredContext:
Use Pappus’ Theorem to find the volume V of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about a line at a distance a (greater than b) from the center of the circle (Figure 5.7.13). By symmetry, the centroid of a circular region is its center. Thus, the distance
traveled by the centroid is 2πa. Since the area of a circle of radius b is πb2, it follows from
Pappus’ Theorem that the volume of the torus is
V = (2πa)(πb2
) = 2π2
ab2

demo_steps.title: Default torus
demo_steps.narration: The circular region of radius b sits a distance a from the vertical axis. Its centroid is the red point, and its full path is the red dashed circle of circumference 2πa.

demo_steps.title: Move the circle farther out
demo_steps.narration: Increasing a expands the red centroid path while leaving the tube thickness unchanged. By Pappus's theorem, both V = 2π²ab² and S = 4π²ab increase in direct proportion to a.

demo_steps.title: Thicken the tube
demo_steps.narration: Increasing b enlarges the generating circle. The surface area increases linearly with b, but the volume increases faster because the generating disk area is πb².

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use world coordinates with the axis of revolution as the +Y vertical axis, +X screen-right at the default view, and +Z depth. Torus centered at origin with symmetry axis along Y. Default major radius a = 2.6 and tube radius b = 0.7; torus parametric surface: x = (a + b cos v) cos u, y = b sin v, z = (a + b cos v) sin u. Overall default torus diameter is about 6.6 units and vertical tube height is 1.4 units. The generating disk is shown at the right side initially, centered at (a, 0, 0), lying in the vertical radial plane z = 0, with radius b. Disk fill pale cream/yellow #ffe3aa at about 0.75 opacity; disk outline blue #139bd7, thickness visibly heavier than dimension lines. Torus body is light gray/silver #d8d8d8 with smooth lighting, subtle darker gray shading at inner rim, and slight transparency or matte shading so the highlighted disk reads as the generating cross-section. Vertical axis is black/dark gray #222222, thin cylinder or line, extending from y = -2.2 to y = 2.2 through x = z = 0. Axis point is black sphere radius about 0.09 at (0,0,0). Centroid point is red #f4545d sphere radius about 0.1 at (a,0,0). Dimension a is a black double-headed arrow from (0,0,0) to (a,0,0), slightly offset toward camera by z = -0.03 so it remains visible, labeled italic 'a' near the center above the arrow. Dimension b is a black double-headed arrow from (a,0,0) to (a+b,0,0), labeled italic 'b' above and to the right. Red centroid path is the circle x = a cos u, y = 0, z = a sin u, rendered dashed in red #f4545d with two or three solid red arrowheads tangent to the path; in the default camera it should resemble the dashed red ellipse in the source. Caption callout is a 2D overlay or billboard near the bottom: cream fill #ffe6b5, gray border #bfbfbf, black text 'The centroid travels\na distance 2πa.' with a broad cream arrow pointing upward toward the lower-right segment of the dashed path. Formula panel should display live values: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab² and S = (2πa)(2πb) = 4π²ab; show current numerical values to 2 decimals.
interactionPlan.notes: Regenerate or rescale the torus mesh, centroid path, generating disk, dimension arrows, and formula values reactively when either slider changes. During the revolve animation, move the highlighted generating disk around the Y-axis with center (a cos θ, 0, a sin θ), rotate its plane so it remains radial, and move the red centroid point with it; keep the dashed red full path visible at all times, optionally brightening the portion already traced. Use smooth Phong or standard material lighting for the gray torus and render labels as billboarding text so they remain readable while dragging the view.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is part of a worked example asking to use Pappus' Theorem to find the volume of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about an axis at distance a from the center of the circle. The figure shows a 3D torus in perspective with the vertical axis of revolution passing through its central hole; the distance a from the axis to the center of the circular cross-section and the radius b of the cross-section are labeled, with the cross-section highlighted as a small circle on the right side of the torus. A red dashed ellipse traces the circular path traveled by the centroid, with direction arrows, and a caption box reads The centroid travels a distance 2pi a. The figure shows that by Pappus' Theorem the volume V = (2 pi a)(pi b^2) = 2 pi^2 a b^2, since the centroid traverses a full circle of circumference 2 pi a as the region revolves.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Sliders for major radius a and tube radius b: reshape the torus in real time and display the updated volume (2π²ab²) and surface area (4π²ab) via Pappus's theorem
- Animate the generating circle of radius b revolving around the axis to show how the torus is formed and trace the red centroid path of length 2πa
- Drag to rotate the 3D torus to inspect its shape from any viewpoint
plan.sourcePath: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.7.13
